title: Run a Stage 5 Science Fair
overview: Bring together everything from Stage 5 Science to run a science fair that teaches visitors the most important ideas from this stage through real investigations.

project.drivingQuestion: How can we use the science from Stage 5 to run an accurate, safe and exciting science fair for our school or community?
project.finalProduct: Create a science-fair plan with a live investigation, labelled displays, a safety checklist, a visitor survey with a data display, and a short explanation of your scientific decisions.

stages.title: 1. Foundations display
stages.prompt: Choose the two most important ideas from Units 1, 2. Build a display that teaches each idea with a model or diagram, an example and a check question.
stages.evidence: Two labelled displays with models, examples and check questions

stages.title: 2. Live investigation
stages.prompt: Pick one investigation from Units 3, 4 and run it live: state your hypothesis, follow the method, record results and explain your conclusion.
stages.evidence: A completed investigation with hypothesis, method, results and conclusion

stages.title: 3. Connections wall
stages.prompt: Create a connections wall that links ideas from Units 5, 6, 7, 8 to everyday life, with at least three labelled connections.
stages.evidence: A connections wall with three labelled links to daily life

stages.title: 4. Present and explain
stages.prompt: Present your science fair. Explain at least three scientific choices, check that your conclusions match your evidence and identify one improvement you would make.
stages.evidence: Spoken, written or recorded scientific explanation

evidenceChecklist: A safety checklist for every activity
A connections wall with three links
A survey with organised data display

rubric.secure: Observations, measurements, models and conclusions are accurate and checked.
Hypotheses, fair testing, recording and conclusions follow the scientific method.
Labels, diagrams, tables or charts make the science visible.
Decisions are explained using appropriate science words and evidence.

questions.question: Which part of a seed is the tiny baby plant?
questions.hint: Use the Unit 1 Science Words reference.
questions.explanation: embryo The embryo is the tiny baby plant; the other parts protect or feed it.

questions.question: A seed that is alive but resting and not growing is said to be:
questions.hint: Use the Unit 1 Science Words reference.
questions.explanation: dormant A dormant seed is alive but resting, waiting for the right conditions.

questions.question: Why do farmers space out their maize plants?
options: so plants do not compete for light and water
questions.answer: so plants do not compete for light and water
questions.hint: Use the Unit 1 Science Words reference.
questions.explanation: so plants do not compete for light and water Crowded plants fight for resources and grow poorly.

questions.question: Which part of a flower produces pollen?
questions.hint: Use the Unit 2 Science Words reference.
questions.explanation: anther. The anther is the pollen-making tip of the stamen.

questions.question: Sepals mainly:
questions.hint: Use the Unit 2 Science Words reference.
questions.explanation: protect the flower bud. Sepals wrap around and guard the bud before it opens.

questions.question: Why do plants spread their seeds far away?
questions.hint: Use the Unit 2 Science Words reference.
questions.explanation: to avoid crowding and competition. Spreading out gives each seed space, light and water.

questions.question: Which state of matter keeps both a definite shape and a definite volume?
questions.hint: Use the Unit 3 Science Words reference.
questions.explanation: solid. Only solids keep both a fixed shape and a fixed volume because their particles are locked in place.

questions.question: Which change needs heat to be REMOVED?
questions.hint: Use the Unit 3 Science Words reference.
questions.explanation: Freezing needs heat removed so particles slow and lock into a solid. The others all need heat added.

questions.question: When sugar is stirred into tea and seems to vanish, it has:
questions.hint: Use the Unit 3 Science Words reference.
questions.explanation: dissolved. The sugar particles spread among the water particles; it is still there (the tea tastes sweet).

questions.question: Which of these is a light source?
questions.hint: Use the Unit 4 Science Words reference.
questions.explanation: a candle flame A candle makes its own light; the others only reflect.

questions.question: A material that lets no light through is:
questions.hint: Use the Unit 4 Science Words reference.
questions.explanation: opaque Opaque means no light passes through.

questions.question: An opaque object in sunlight makes a:
questions.hint: Use the Unit 4 Science Words reference.
questions.explanation: dark sharp shadow Opaque objects block all the light.

questions.question: A shadow forms when light is blocked by:
questions.hint: Use the Unit 5 Science Words reference.
questions.explanation: an opaque object. Only opaque materials block light fully to make a clear shadow; transparent things let light pass.

questions.question: As you move a torch closer to an object, its shadow gets:
questions.hint: Use the Unit 5 Science Words reference.
questions.explanation: larger. A close light spreads over the object more, so the shadow grows.

questions.question: The shadow of a stick moves through the day mainly because:
questions.hint: Use the Unit 5 Science Words reference.
questions.explanation: the Earth turns. The Earth's spin makes the sun appear to move, changing the shadow.

questions.question: What is at the centre of our Solar System?
questions.hint: Use the Unit 6 Science Words reference.
questions.explanation: the Sun. The Sun sits at the centre and everything else orbits it.

questions.question: Which planet do we live on?
questions.hint: Use the Unit 6 Science Words reference.
questions.explanation: the third. Earth is the third planet out from the Sun.

questions.question: About how many days does the Moon take to complete all its phases?
questions.hint: Use the Unit 6 Science Words reference.
questions.explanation: 29.5. The full cycle of phases takes about 29.5 days.

questions.question: A force is best described as:
questions.hint: The definition is four words long.
questions.explanation: A force is a push or a pull, and it is measured in newtons.

questions.question: A book lies still on a table. Which is true?
options: Two balanced forces act on it
Only the table pushes on it
questions.answer: Two balanced forces act on it
questions.hint: Ask what the book would do with no table.
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls it down and the table pushes up by exactly as much. The book is still because the forces cancel, not because there are none.

questions.question: A force diagram shows a 5 N arrow down and a 5 N arrow up. The object is:
questions.hint: Balanced forces say something about CHANGE, not about being still.
questions.explanation: Equal opposite arrows mean balanced forces, so the motion does not change. That covers standing still and moving at a steady speed alike - the diagram cannot tell you which.

questions.question: Which food group is the body's main source of energy?
questions.hint: Rice, maize and cassava all belong to it.
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are the body's main fuel and make up the largest part of most meals.
questions.unitTitle: Food, Digestion and a Healthy Diet

questions.question: Digestion is completed in:
questions.hint: It is also where the nutrients enter the blood.
questions.explanation: The stomach churns and softens; digestion finishes in the small intestine, where the nutrients pass into the blood.
questions.unitTitle: Food, Digestion and a Healthy Diet

questions.question: An animal's intestine is thirty times its body length. It most likely eats:
questions.hint: Which kind of food gives up its nutrients most slowly?
questions.explanation: Plant material is tough and slow to break down, so plant eaters need very long guts. Meat eaters manage with about four times their body length.
questions.unitTitle: Food, Digestion and a Healthy Diet
